comparisons.peer_summary: Other investments included in the fair value measurements consisted of insurance annuity contracts of $432 million and $404 million, and other various investments of $31 million and $71 million at December 31, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citigroup and Bank of America report specific balances for insurance annuity contracts or long-duration policyholder liabilities in their Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements, though the accounting treatment and line items differ. Citigroup specifically isolates a liability for future policyholder benefits for Mexican annuity contracts (approx. $413 million in 2024) within Legacy Franchises, with changes reflected in AOCI and the balance recorded in 'Other liabilities'. Bank of America reports 'insurance annuity contracts' as part of 'Other investments' within fair value measurements ($432 million in 2024), without explicitly detailing AOCI adjustments for policyholder benefit liabilities in this specific summary. While both address insurance-related financial instruments, Citigroup's disclosure focuses on the actuarial liability and AOCI impact for long-duration contracts, whereas Bank of America's disclosure frames the annuity contracts as investment assets in plan assets.
